question.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation $3{x}_{1}^{2}+10{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}=32?$
question.worked_solution:
Consider the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+10{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}.$ To determine the curve defined by the given equation, we reduce $Q(x)$ to its canonical (diagonal) form.  

First, we write down the matrix of $Q(x),$ which is

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we find the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 5 \\ 5 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda -16 & =0 \\ \lambda  & =8,\,-2\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, our quadratic form can be reduced to $8{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}^{2}.$  

In the new variables, the curve has the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}8{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}^{2} & =32 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This is a hyperbola with semiaxes  $2$ and $4.$
